title.en: The blue planet and our address

text.en: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, the first Indian to reach the International Space Station, said the Earth looks completely one, with no borders visible.

From high in space the Earth looks tiny and we cannot see our city or village, only the broad shapes of land and sea on our blue planet.
Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma, the first Indian to see the Earth from space, was asked how India looked from above. He replied with the line Saare Jahaan Se Achcha, the best in the world.
We all have an address: name, house number or building, street, village, town or city, district, state or union territory, country, and planet.
Use a globe to find whether all the oceans are connected and where India is.
From above we do not see borders. Nature has no boundaries, so air, water, clouds, seeds and animals move freely across the world.
Just as people across India share mangoes, rivers and festivals, people across the world are linked by what we share. Our clothes, food and toys may come from different parts of the world.
Everything is linked through nature, trade, travel and the ways we care for the planet together. Earth is our shared home.
DIGIPIN is a digital address giving every small place in India its own 10-character code, helping postmen, ambulances and deliveries find you faster.
Story: rosy starlings, pink and black birds, fly thousands of kilometres every winter from southern Russia and Mongolia to India, and eat locusts and grasshoppers, which helps farmers.

problem.en: Write the parts of an address down to the planet.

prompt.en: What does 'nature has no boundaries' mean?

requiredIdeas.en: Birds, air and water cross borders
Rosy starlings fly from Russia to India
Earth looks like one from space

points.en: From space the Earth looks one planet without borders.
Air, water and animals move freely.
Rosy starlings link Russia and India.
